In [[functional analysis]] and related areas of [[mathematics]], an '''ultrabarrelled space''' is a [[topological vector spaces]] (TVS) for which every ultrabarrel is a [[Neighbourhood (topology)|neighbourhood]] of the origin. 

== Definition ==

A subset <math>B_0</math> of a TVS <math>X</math> is called an '''ultrabarrel ''' if it is a closed and [[balanced set|balanced]] subset of <math>X</math> and if there exists a sequence <math>\left(B_i\right)_{i=1}^{\infty}</math> of closed balanced and [[absorbing set|absorbing]] subsets of <math>X</math> such that <math>B_{i+1} + B_{i+1} \subseteq B_i</math> for all <math>i = 0, 1, \ldots.</math> 
In this case, <math>\left(B_i\right)_{i=1}^{\infty}</math> is called a '''defining sequence''' for <math>B_0.</math> 
A TVS <math>X</math> is called '''ultrabarrelled''' if every ultrabarrel in <math>X</math> is a [[Neighbourhood (topology)|neighbourhood]] of the origin.{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|pp=65-76}} 

== Properties ==

A [[locally convex]] ultrabarrelled space is a [[barrelled space]].{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|pp=65-76}} 
Every ultrabarrelled space is a [[quasi-ultrabarrelled space]].{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|pp=65-76}}

== Examples and sufficient conditions ==

Complete and metrizable TVSs are ultrabarrelled.{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|pp=65-76}} 
If <math>X</math> is a complete [[locally bounded]] non-locally convex TVS and if <math>B_0</math> is a closed [[Balanced set|balanced]] and bounded neighborhood of the origin, then <math>B_0</math> is an ultrabarrel that is not [[Convex set|convex]] and has a defining sequence consisting of non-convex sets.{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|pp=65-76}} 

=== Counter-examples ===

There exist [[barrelled space]]s that are not ultrabarrelled.{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|pp=65-76}} 
There exist TVSs that are complete and metrizable (and thus ultrabarrelled) but not barrelled.{{sfn|Khaleelulla|1982|pp=65-76}}
